- Properties: `settle_s`, `routing` (last selected). Operates only on managed
  lines and never calls `qsw.reset()`.

Module helper `target_state(lines, breakouts, routing)` → sorted `(line, tap)`
closures (pure; for tests/review).
# `sharpelab_nb.drivers` API Reference

Instrument drivers in `src/sharpelab_nb/drivers/`, re-exported from the package:

```python
from sharpelab_nb.drivers import SRS_DC205, Yokogawa7651, ANC350
```

The `drivers` package (`src/drivers/`: `FastBi1K5`, `QSwitch`, `ContactMux`,
the VTI `SRS_DC205`, …) is documented separately in
[`drivers.md`](drivers.md).

---

## `SRS_DC205` — DC voltage source (fixed-duration ramp)

`SRS_DC205(name, address, *, ramp_num_points=100, ramp_wait_time=0.01, **kwargs)`.
Serial `VisaInstrument` (115200 baud).

| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voltage` | V | R/W | raw setpoint (7 dp) |
| `smart_voltage` | V | R/W | set → `ramp_voltage` |
| `voltage_range` | — | R/W | 0: ±1 V, 1: ±10 V, 2: ±100 V |
| `output` | 0/1 | R/W | output enable |

- **`ramp_voltage(volt)`** — software ramp from the current reading over
  `ramp_num_points` steps spaced `ramp_wait_time` apart (so the duration is
  roughly fixed regardless of ΔV), **plus a mandatory 10 s settle when
  `|Δvolt| > 0.1 V`**. (The VTI `drivers.SRS_DC205` of the same name uses
  rate-based (`ramp_rate` V/s) semantics and has no fixed settle — they are not
  interchangeable.)

---

## `Yokogawa7651` — programmable DC source (pre-SCPI, write-only cached)

`Yokogawa7651(name, address, *, coil_constant=None, **kwargs)`. The 7651 is
pre-SCPI (no `*IDN?`) and cannot report programmed values back over the bus, so
**all set parameters are write-only with a software cache**.

| parameter | unit | R/W | range / notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `volt` | V | W | ±30 V |
| `current` | A | W | ±0.12 A |
| `field` | T | W | requires `coil_constant=`; range = ±0.12·|coil| |
| `mode` | — | W | `'VOLT'` (F1;) / `'CURR'` (F5;) |
| `output` | bool | W | output enable |

- After a kernel restart the cache is empty, so the ramp methods raise unless
  the cache is seeded first: **`set_voltage_cache(value)`** /
  **`set_current_cache(value)`**, or pass `start=` to the ramp call.
- **`ramp_voltage(target, step=0.01, delay=0.05, start=None)`** /
  **`ramp_current(target, step=0.001, delay=0.05, start=None)`** — software ramp
  from the cached (or `start=`) value; `step` must be `> 0`.
- When `coil_constant` is given, `field.step`/`field.inter_delay` are
  pre-configured for safe ramping (0.1 mT / 0.1 s ⇒ ~1 mT/s).
- `trigger()` sends `E;` (normally automatic after each set). `get_idn()`
  returns a static dict.

---

## `ANC350` — attocube piezo motion controller (rotator)

`ANC350(name, dll_dir, *, device_no=0, num_axes=3, **kwargs)`. Loads
`anc350v2.dll`/`libusb0.dll` from `dll_dir`; exposes `num_axes` axes as a
`ChannelTuple` at `.axes` (each an `ANC350Axis`).

### `ANC350Axis` (one stepper axis)
| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | — | R | raw status int (decode via `is_moving`/`is_at_eot`/`has_sensor_error`/`is_sensor_disconnected`) |
| `position` | counts | R | raw sensor int32 (INT32_MAX when sensor power is off — the toploader default) |
| `rotation_count` | — | R | full-rotation counter |
| `amplitude` | mV | R/W | step drive amplitude, 0–70 000 |
| `frequency` | Hz | R/W | step frequency, 1–2000 |
| `dc_level` | mV | R/W | constant DC for fine positioning (output must be enabled) |
| `output_enabled` | bool | W | HV output; reads a software tri-state cache (True/False/None) — `set_output_cache()` to seed after restart |

Methods: `step(direction, count=1, *, wait=True, timeout=60.0, poll_interval=0.05)`
(±1 = forward/backward), `step_continuous(direction)`, `stop()`,
`wait_until_idle(…)`. `step`/`step_continuous` refuse to run unless the output
cache is `True`.

---

## Lock-in servo (`lockin_servo`)

Closed-loop positioning of an `ANC350Axis` against a lock-in voltage readback.
Not re-exported from the package — import from
`sharpelab_nb.drivers.lockin_servo`.

### `bring_up_servo_axis(name, axis, readback, *, amplitude_mv=60_000, frequency_hz=100, direction_sign=None, settle_time=0.5, v_min=-50e-3, v_max=+50e-3, tolerance=25e-6, max_iterations=200, step_count=1)` → `LockinServoedAxis`
One-call bring-up: set amplitude/frequency, enable HV output, resolve
`direction_sign` (if `None`, **physically steps the rotator** via
`calibrate_direction_sign` and prints the result to cache), and construct the
servo. `amplitude_mv` is millivolts (60 000 = 60 V).

### `LockinServoedAxis(name, *, axis, readback, direction_sign, v_min, v_max, tolerance=25e-6, settle_time=0.5, max_iterations=200, step_count=1)`
| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voltage` | V | R | one-shot read of the underlying readback |
| `target_voltage` | V | R/W | **set runs the servo loop synchronously**; get = last target (or None) |
| `last_iterations` | — | R | iterations used by the last run |
| `last_residual` | V | R | `abs(target − final)` of the last run |

`set` of `target_voltage` raises `ServoTimeout` if `max_iterations` is exceeded.
`abort()` requests the in-progress loop to stop (does not call `axis.stop()`).
`direction_sign` and `axis` are properties.

### `thermalized_setpoint(servo, readback_lockin, *, name=None, full_amp=None, off_amp=0.004, wait_s=60.0)` → `Parameter`
Wrap a servo move + sensor-excitation cool-down into one settable-only
`Parameter` (use as a sweep's slow axis): restore excitation → servo to target
→ drop excitation to `off_amp` → wait `wait_s` for the stage to thermalize.
After each set the lock-in amplitude is left at `off_amp`, so the followed
readback is noise during the read window — the meaningful axis is the setpoint.

### `calibrate_direction_sign(axis, readback, *, settle_time, noise_samples=5, noise_threshold=None, max_test_steps=10)` → `(sign, n_steps)`
Resolve step polarity empirically: issue forward steps until `readback` moves
past the noise threshold, return `+1` if it rose else `-1` (with the step count
used). `settle_time` is required. Called automatically by `bring_up_servo_axis`
when `direction_sign=None`.

## HERA — Step 3: SdH spot check, electron side (`sdh-spot-check`), n = +3.2×10¹² at D = 0, B 0 → 10 T

Calibration from run 5 (ana): c_bg/c_tg = 0.773 (data), c_tg = 2.796 mF/m² (9.5 nm prior), n_offset −0.089×10¹², D_offset −0.013 V/nm (R_CNP(D) symmetry). # === SdH spot check, electron side (`sdh-spot-check`): n = +3.2e12 at D = 0 (region-A calibration), B 0 -> 10 T ===
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD

# --- session calibration from run 5 (cnp-and-dline-calibration; ratio data-calibrated, scale = geometry prior) ---
CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
n_spot, D_spot = 3.2, 0.0                       # 1e12 cm^-2, V/nm
Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot = calc_gate_voltages(n_spot, D_spot, CAL["c_tg"], CAL["c_bg"], CAL["n_offset"], CAL["D_offset"])
assert TG_MIN <= Vtg_spot <= TG_MAX and BG_MIN <= Vbg_spot <= BG_MAX, (Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot)
print(f"spot: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm -> (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}) V; "
      f"roundtrip n,D = {calc_nD(Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot, CAL['c_tg'], CAL['c_bg'], CAL['n_offset'], CAL['D_offset'])}")

# --- preconditions (assumed, not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0, _B0 = T_sample(), magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (|B|<0.05: sweep starts at 0), V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (0), "
      f"PS heater {magnet.persistent_switch_on()}, output {magnet.output_enabled()}")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5 and abs(_B0) < 0.05 and abs(k_si()) < 0.01
assert magnet.persistent_switch_on() and magnet.output_enabled()

# --- field grid: uniform in B (blocking rate-limited magnet). 50 mT to 1 T (background only), 10 mT 1 -> 10 T:
B_vec = np.unique(np.round(np.hstack((np.arange(0.0, 1.0, 0.05), np.arange(1.0, 10.0001, 0.01))), 4))
assert B_vec.max() <= B_SESSION_CAP
I_TRIP = 1e-9
# Fixed sensitivity: 50 uV = 5 kOhm full scale at 10 nA (R(B=0) ~ 70 Ohm = 1.4 % FS; MR + SdH maxima at high B size the headroom).
sr1.sensitivity(50e-6)
print(f"B grid: {len(B_vec)} pts, {B_vec[0]} -> {B_vec[-1]} T; sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V, tau {sr1.time_constant()} s (settle_s {magnet.settle_s} s = dwell)")

mc = dict(meas_config); mc["Si (V)"] = k_si(); mc["sample_temperature:"] = _T0
mc["comments"] = f"sdh-spot-check electron: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm (run-5 cal), (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}), B 0 -> 10 T, 10 mT above 1 T, sr1 50 uV"
s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
s.add_comment('sdh-spot-check')
s.add_comment(f'electron side: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12 cm^-2, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm; (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}); '
              f'B 0 -> 10 T uniform-B (50 mT to 1 T, 10 mT above); cal run 5: ratio {CAL["c_bg"]/CAL["c_tg"]:.3f}, n_offset {CAL["n_offset"]:+.3f}e12, D_offset {CAL["D_offset"]:+.3f}')
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, Vbg_spot); s.ramp(k_tg.volt, Vtg_spot)
interruptible_sleep(10)

# row layout: [time, B, T_sample, k_tg.curr, k_bg.curr, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
s.plot(magnet.field, sr1.X); s.plot(magnet.field, sr0.X); s.plot('time', k_tg.curr); s.plot('time', k_bg.curr)

def leak_guard(station, data):
    i_tg, i_bg = abs(float(data[3])), abs(float(data[4]))
    if i_tg > I_TRIP or i_bg > I_TRIP:
        print(f"LEAK TRIP at B={float(data[1]):+.3f} T: |I_tg|={i_tg:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg:.3e} A")
        station.interrupt_requested = True
s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

s.sweep(magnet.field, B_vec, delay=0)
# gates stay at the spot; field stays at 10 T (the hole-side spot check rides it down) — no park here.
print(f"done: B = {magnet.field():+.3f} T, (Vtg, Vbg) = ({k_tg.volt():+.4f}, {k_bg.volt():+.4f})")

## Run 5 — 0 T gatemap (`gatemap`) → `cnp-and-dline-calibration`

Raw map (log R, TG fast [−0.3, +1.0] × BG slow [−1.3, +1.2], 20 × 40 mV, sr1 100 µV; run 4 was the same map aborted at 3 min when the ridge railed at 2 kΩ). **Read:** one dominant CNP ridge (A) running from (V_tg, V_bg) ≈ (+1.0, −1.3) to (−0.3, +0.45), plus a fainter **parallel** ridge (B) ≈ 0.19 V lower in V_tg — the second peak of runs 0–3. Ridge A's resistance is 240 Ω near D ≈ 0 and grows to ~2.4 kΩ at raw D ≈ +0.25 V/nm (saturating beyond), i.e. a D-tunable gap; **not a stacking read** (investigation Step 1 addendum: three candidate parents). Fits (ridge position = V_tg vs V_bg rows, so −slope = c_bg/c_tg): ridge A in the operating window |V_bg| < 0.5: slope −0.773 (rms 19 mV); high-D rows: −0.763 (rms 6 mV); ridge B: −0.69 (8 rows, rms 13 mV). **Calibration:** ratio c_bg/c_tg = 0.773 (data-calibrated; prior 0.864, −11 % — plausible hBN-thickness error, not a transposition); c_tg anchored at the 9.5 nm prior (absolute scale = geometry prior, pending a lever-arm check); n_offset = −0.089×10¹²; **D_offset from the R_CNP(D) symmetry** (vertex of the ridge-A resistance minimum, ≈ +0.012 raw) — the one feature that physically locates D = 0. Region B is electron-doped by 0.43×10¹² relative to A: a series-mosaic confound (same template expected, 13 % higher n at the fan density — extra tones at ×1.13). Realized D = 0 window inside the validators: **n = −1.27 … +3.27×10¹²** (TG-limited on both ends). Channel arithmetic: R = (sr1_X/1)/(sr0_X/−1e6).

      f"PS heater {magnet.persistent_switch_on()}, output {magnet.output_enabled()}")

def sanitize_tg_bg(vtg_vec, vbg_vec, tg_lims, bg_lims):
    """
    Given a list of tg and bg voltages, removes any points which are outside tg_lims and bg_lims
    """
    vtg_new_vec = []
    vbg_new_vec = []
    for ind in range(len(vtg_vec)):
        vtg, vbg = vtg_vec[ind], vbg_vec[ind]
        if vtg < tg_lims[0] or vtg > tg_lims[1] or vbg < bg_lims[0] or vbg > bg_lims[1]:
            pass
        else:
            vtg_new_vec.append(vtg)
            vbg_new_vec.append(vbg)
    return np.array(vtg_new_vec), np.array(vbg_new_vec)

def sanitize_tg_bg(vtg_vec, vbg_vec, tg_lims, bg_lims):
    """
    Given a list of tg and bg voltages, removes any points which are outside tg_lims and bg_lims
    """
    vtg_new_vec = []
    vbg_new_vec = []
    for ind in range(len(vtg_vec)):
        vtg, vbg = vtg_vec[ind], vbg_vec[ind]
        if vtg < tg_lims[0] or vtg > tg_lims[1] or vbg < bg_lims[0] or vbg > bg_lims[1]:
            pass
        else:
            vtg_new_vec.append(vtg)
            vbg_new_vec.append(vbg)
    return np.array(vtg_new_vec), np.array(vbg_new_vec)

## HERA — Step 1: first 0 T gatemap (`gatemap`) → CNP line + (n, D) calibration

Gate C passed (runs 0–3: alive, no leakage, Rxx 60–330 Ω). The map settles whether they are parallel CNP ridges (two flake domains, same lever arms) or not, fits the ridge slope for the capacitance ratio (`cnp-and-dline-calibration`), and locates the D = 0 line. Window: TG fast over its full range [−0.3, +1.0] V at 20 mV (66 pts); BG slow [−1.3, +1.2] V at 40 mV (63 rows). Coverage trade: BG is stopped at +1.2 V rather than the +2.0 V limit — from the prior, the region-A CNP line exits the TG window at V_bg ≈ +0.1 and the D = 0 line reaches V_tg = 1.0 at V_bg ≈ 1.16, so [1.2, 2.0] is metallic electron-side at finite D only, ~35 min for nothing the calibration or the fan needs. Sensitivity fixed at 20 µV (2 kΩ full scale — ×6 over the largest peak seen; a rail along the ridge at large |D| would itself be a read). Dwell: fast_delay 1 s against τ = 0.3 s / 24 dB (≈3τ — a uniform lag on a slope read, shifts the ridge intercept by ≲ 1 step, slope untouched); slow_delay 3 s. ```python
# === Gate C — liveness + gross gate safety: gate-current-sanity-check (first-session branch) ===
# Four legs, each gate 0 -> each card limit with the other parked at 0, 101 pts, delay 1 s,
# nplci=10 on the gate-current channels (pA floor). Lock-in X on sr1 (B_1-B_2) + sr0 (drain)
# answer "is the device alive on the provided contacts"; gate currents answer "is it safe".
# Automatic abort: |I_gate| > 1 nA on either Keithley trips the sweep (no operator eyes in E1).
from sharpelab_nb.autorange import autorange_sr830s

# --- preconditions (state this cell assumes but does not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0 = T_sample(); _B0 = magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (expect 1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (expect |B|<0.02), "
      f"V_tg = {k_tg.volt():+.3f}, V_bg = {k_bg.volt():+.3f}, V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (expect 0)")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5, f"T_sample {_T0} K off base"
assert abs(_B0) < 0.02, f"magnet not at zero: {_B0} T"
assert abs(k_si()) < 0.01, "Si gate not at 0"

legs = [(k_tg, TG_MAX), (k_tg, TG_MIN), (k_bg, BG_MAX), (k_bg, BG_MIN)]
n_pts, delay = 101, 1.0
I_TRIP = 1e-9   # A — hard abort threshold on either gate current

# pA-floor readback on the gate-current channels (reset at the end if no leg tripped)
k_tg.nplci(10); k_bg.nplci(10)

# sr1 sensitivity sized for an unknown Rxx: 500 uV = 50 kOhm full scale at I_bias = 10 nA
# (drive 1 V / 100 MOhm, as the operator set it); autorange hook tracks from there.
sr1.sensitivity(500e-6)
print(f"drive {sr1.amplitude()} V @ {sr1.frequency()} Hz -> I_bias ~ {sr1.amplitude()/100e6*1e9:.1f} nA; "
      f"sr0 sens {sr0.sensitivity()} V, sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V, tau {sr1.time_constant()} s")

tripped = []
for gate, v_end in legs:
    other = k_bg if gate is k_tg else k_tg
    mc = dict(meas_config); mc["comments"] = f"gate-current-sanity-check: {gate.name} 0 -> {v_end:+g} V, other gate 0, Si 0, B 0"
    s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)

usage: nb-collab [-h]
                 {append,edit-cell,execute-cell,exec-all,delete-cell,wait,interrupt}
                 ...

nb-collab — drop cells into a JupyterLab-open notebook over the YDoc/RTC
channel.

positional arguments:
  {append,edit-cell,execute-cell,exec-all,delete-cell,wait,interrupt}
    append              Append cells to a live notebook (notebook must be
                        served by a running JupyterLab).
    edit-cell           Replace an existing cell's source (policy-gated;
                        requires edit_no_exec or edit_exec).
    execute-cell        Run an existing code cell against the notebook's
                        kernel (policy=append_exec or edit_exec).
    exec-all            Run every code cell in document order on one kernel
                        (policy=append_exec or edit_exec).
    delete-cell         Remove an existing cell by id (policy=edit_exec only).
    wait                Wait for a specific cell to finish executing.
    interrupt           Interrupt the notebook's kernel (the abort lever for
                        autonomous sweeps).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
====
usage: nb-collab append [-h] [--markdown TEXT] [--code TEXT]
                        [--markdown-file PATH] [--code-file PATH]
                        [--summary TEXT] [--eta DURATION] [--execute | --wait]
                        [--follow] [--server-url SERVER_URL] [--token TOKEN]
                        [--settle SETTLE] [--timeout TIMEOUT] [--poll POLL]
                        notebook

Appends markdown and/or code cells at the end of a JupyterLab-open notebook
via the YDoc/RTC channel. Inserted cells are tagged metadata.hera (a dict
carrying the version tag and an appended_at UTC timestamp) so they can be
filtered and timed later. Re-running with the same args double-inserts.

positional arguments:
  notebook              Path to .ipynb (absolute or relative to cwd).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --markdown TEXT       Append a markdown cell with this source. Pass '-' to
                        read the cell from stdin; multiple '-' flags consume
                        successive chunks separated by a line of '---|'.
                        Repeatable; order preserved across all
                        --markdown/--code variants.
  --code TEXT           Append an un-executed code cell with this source. Pass
                        '-' to read the cell from stdin (see --markdown for
                        chunk semantics). Repeatable; order preserved across
                        all --markdown/--code variants.
  --markdown-file PATH  Append a markdown cell whose source is read from PATH
                        (UTF-8). Repeatable; order-preserved.
  --code-file PATH      Append an un-executed code cell whose source is read
                        from PATH (UTF-8). Repeatable; order-preserved.
  --summary TEXT        One-line dense spec of the proposed measurement.
                        Rendered into the FIRST appended markdown cell, right
                        after its leading heading (or prepended if the cell
                        has none) as a timestamped blockquote: '> **14:32** ·
                        <summary>' — the clock is server-local time at append;
                        _/* in the text are escaped for rendering. Also
                        stamped verbatim to metadata.hera.summary on that
                        cell. Requires at least one markdown cell among the
                        appended cells (--markdown/--markdown-file); must not
                        contain a backtick. At most once.
  --eta DURATION        Expected runtime for the proposed measurement — '40m',
                        '2h', or '1h30m' (optional <N>h then optional <N>m, h
                        before m; at least one required, total > 0; fractional
                        values rejected). A bare number like '40' is REJECTED
                        — add the m/h suffix. Rendered into the FIRST appended
                        markdown cell's blockquote line (with --summary or
                        alone) as '**ETA ~15:12** (≈40 min)' in server-local
                        time, computed from the same append instant; crossing
                        local midnight adds ' (+1d)' right after the clock.
                        Also stamped as an ISO-8601 UTC instant to
                        metadata.hera.eta_at on that cell, and echoed to
                        stdout as 'eta: ~15:12 (≈40 min)'. Requires at least
                        one markdown cell among the appended cells. At most
                        once.
  --execute             After appending, run the last appended code cell
                        YOURSELF by the id this append just created (never
                        nb['cells'][-1] off the stale on-disk file). Policy-
                        gated like execute-cell (append_exec or edit_exec),
                        checked before any cell lands. Exit code reflects the
                        cell's status. Mutually exclusive with --wait.
====
usage: hera-watch [-h] [--next] [--once] [--poll POLL] [--timeout TIMEOUT]
                  [--follow] [--wait-start WAIT_START] [--channels CHANNELS]
                  [--raw] [--bias-current BIAS_CURRENT] [--every EVERY]
                  [--fs-warn FS_WARN] [--leak-excess-warn LEAK_EXCESS_WARN]
                  run_dir

Live run-dir digest: one line per landed sweep row (gain-divided Rxx/I stats +
progress/ETA) for an agent to tail.

positional arguments:
  run_dir               sweep run directory (contains metadata.json +
                        data.tsv). May not exist yet — the watch waits up to
                        --wait-start for it to appear. With --next, give a
                        data/ dir instead.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --next                treat run_dir as a data/ dir and latch onto the NEXT
                        run to appear (arm before the cell runs). Robust to
                        2nd+ runs and lowest-free-id allocation — snapshots
                        existing runs, waits for a new one.
  --once                digest current state then exit (no watch loop)
  --poll POLL           poll interval in seconds while watching (default 5)
  --timeout TIMEOUT     stop the measurement watch after this many seconds
                        (default 570, sub-CC-Bash-cap). See --follow.
  --follow              watch to completion with no deadline (multi-hour
                        runs); overrides --timeout. Use with a backgrounded
                        invocation.
  --wait-start WAIT_START
                        if run_dir doesn't exist yet, wait up to this many
                        seconds for it to appear (default 1800; <=0 waits
                        indefinitely)
  --channels CHANNELS   comma-separated lock-in channels to include (e.g.
                        sr1,sr2). Default: all.
  --raw                 report raw lock-in X (skip gain division). Escape
                        hatch.
  --bias-current BIAS_CURRENT
                        override I_bias in amps (default:
                        bias_voltage/bias_resistor from metadata)
  --every EVERY         1D sweeps: emit a digest line every N new rows
                        (default 25)
  --fs-warn FS_WARN     warn when a lock-in's max|X| reaches this fraction of
                        its full-scale sensitivity (default 0.90; SR830 rails
                        ~1.09×). Requires sensitivity in the instrument
                        snapshot.
  --leak-excess-warn LEAK_EXCESS_WARN
                        warn when a gate current's excess over its baseline
                        (max|I - I0|) reaches this many amps on 2+ consecutive
                        points (default 100e-12 = 100 pA)

"""Scratch: SdH read of spot checks run 6 (electron, n=+3.2e12) and run 7 (hole, n=-1.2e12)."""
import numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, sdh_fft, sdh_onset, SdhOnsetError, luttinger_frequency

def load(i):
    r = open_run(f"data/{i}")
    B = r.col("magnet_field"); I = r.col("sr0_X")/(-1e6); R = r.col("sr1_X")/I
    o = np.argsort(B); return B[o], R[o], r

fig, axs = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
for k, (rid, n12) in enumerate([(6, 3.2), (7, -1.2)]):
    B, R, r = load(rid)
    FL = luttinger_frequency(abs(n12)*1e16)
    print(f"\n=== run {rid}: n = {n12:+.2f}e12, F_L (single FS, g=4) = {FL:.2f} T; pts {len(B)}, B {B.min():.2f}-{B.max():.2f}")
    axs[0, k].plot(B, R, lw=0.7); axs[0, k].set_title(f"run {rid} raw Rxx, n={n12:+.1f}e12 D=0"); axs[0, k].set_xlabel("B (T)"); axs[0, k].set_ylabel("Rxx (Ohm)")
    m = B > 0.29
    axs[1, k].plot(1/B[m], R[m], lw=0.7); axs[1, k].set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); axs[1, k].set_xlim(0, 1/1.0)
    # onset
    try:
        on = sdh_onset(R, B, r_full_scale=50e-6/10e-9)
        print(on.summary())
    except SdhOnsetError as e:
        print("sdh_onset failed:", e)
    # FFT in windows
    for (blo, bhi), c in [((1.0, 4.0), "C0"), ((1.5, 6.0), "C1"), ((2.0, 10.0), "C2"), ((4.0, 10.0), "C3")]:
        mm = (B >= blo) & (B <= bhi)
        if mm.sum() < 20: continue
        f, sp = sdh_fft(R[mm][:, None], B[mm], bg_degree=4, log=False, nfft=2048)
        sp = sp[0]; sel = (f > 1) & (f < 80)
        pk = f[sel][np.argsort(sp[sel])[::-1][:6]]
        print(f"  FFT window {blo}-{bhi} T: top peaks (T): {np.round(np.sort(pk),2)}")
        axs[2, k].plot(f, sp/sp[sel].max(), c, lw=0.8, label=f"{blo}-{bhi} T")
    axs[2, k].axvline(FL, color="k", ls="--", lw=0.8, label=f"F_L={FL:.1f}")
    for frac in (0.25, 0.5, 0.75): axs[2, k].axvline(FL*frac, color="gray", ls=":", lw=0.6)
    axs[2, k].set_xlim(0, 60); axs[2, k].set_xlabel("F (T)"); axs[2, k].legend(fontsize=7)
    # minima positions (candidates for QH) at high B
    from scipy.signal import find_peaks, savgol_filter
    mm = B > 1.0
    Rs = savgol_filter(R[mm], 7, 2)
    mins, _ = find_peaks(-Rs, prominence=max(5, 0.05*Rs.max()))
    Bm = B[mm][mins]
    nu_geo = abs(n12)*1e16*6.62607e-34/(1.602e-19*Bm)
    print("  Rxx minima (B, R, nu_geo-cal):", [(round(b,2), round(float(v),1), round(float(nu),1)) for b, v, nu in zip(Bm, Rs[mins], nu_geo) if b > 1.5])
    print("  Rxx maxima B>4 T:", np.round(B[mm][find_peaks(Rs, prominence=max(10, 0.1*Rs.max()))[0]], 2))
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/sdh_spots.png", dpi=110)
print("saved hera_scratch/sdh_spots.png")

# vti-02 — stacking-order campaign plan (HERA)

*Goal: ABAB vs ABCA vs ABCB for tetralayer vti-02, region-resolved (one wired pair: sr1 = B_1−B_2), evidence-cited. Written 2026-08-23 ~05:30 by the second instance (the first instance's plan file was not on disk — reconstructed from its cell markdowns, session_notes and the data).*

## What discriminates the stackings (what the fan must show)

| observable | ABAB (Bernal) | ABCA (rhombohedral) | ABCB (mixed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| low-energy bands at D = 0 | two bilayer-like parabolic bands (light + heavy), band overlap → semimetal | one flat quartic band, E ∝ k⁴ | monolayer-like linear + trilayer-like cubic, offset |
| SdH at fixed n | **two** fundamental tones, F₁+F₂ = n·h/4e | **one** tone at n·h/4e (heavy → weak at T_e ≈ 8 K) | two tones, very different masses; Lifshitz transition vs n |
| zero-mode LL count (total) | 16, split 8 + 8 between blocks | 16 in one ladder (N = 0..3) | 16 = 4 (mono) + 12 (ABC-trilayer) |
| strong QH gaps at low B | ν = ±8 (block gap) and multiples of 4; level crossings between blocks | ν = ±16 first; ν = ±4, ±8, ±12 from splitting the N = 0..3 manifold | ν = ±4 (Dirac N = 0) and ±12, ±16 |
| ν = 0 at D = 0, high B | insulating (layer-antiferro/quantum-Hall ferro) | insulating | weak |
| CNP gap vs D | opens (bilayer-like), both blocks | opens strongly (flat band → largest R) | asymmetric in D |

The Landau fan (Rxx vs n and B at D = 0) delivers items 2–4 at once; the 0 T gatemap (run 5) already gave the D-dependence of R_CNP (gap opens with D — three candidate parents, not discriminating on its own).

## Steps

1. **Gate C / liveness** (`gate-current-sanity-check`, runs 0–3) — DONE. Alive on the provided pair, no leakage to any limit, Rxx 60–330 Ω; two series regions (double peaks).
2. **0 T gatemap → CNP + (n, D) calibration** (`gatemap`, run 4 aborted / run 5) — DONE. Ridge A (main) slope → c_bg/c_tg = 0.773; c_tg anchored at the 9.5 nm prior; n_offset −0.089×10¹², D_offset −0.013 V/nm (R_CNP(D) vertex). Ridge B = second region, 0.43×10¹² more electron-doped (series mosaic confound). D = 0 line inside the validators: n = −1.27 … +3.27×10¹² (TG-limited).
3. **SdH spot checks at D = 0** (`sdh-spot-check`, runs 6 electron +3.2, 7 hole −1.2) — DONE (measured), read in ana on 08-23. Clear SdH from ~1 T on both sides, QH minima (Rxx → 0) by 2.3 T at n_geo = 3.2. Electron side Δν = 4 periodicity at F ≈ 29.5 T vs F_L(geo) = 33.1 → **density scale ≈ 10 % high** (c_tg prior too large) — the fan's LL indexing recalibrates the absolute scale. Broad Rxx maximum 7.8–9.5 T at n_geo 3.2 (level crossing / gap collapse candidate).
4. **Landau fan at D = 0** (`landau-fan`) — **NEXT** (operator's request). n fast along the calibrated D = 0 line, −1.25 … +3.2×10¹² at 0.025 (179 pts); B slow 0.5 → 4.0 T at 0.1 T then 4.2 → 10 T at 0.2 T (66 rows), magnet starts at 0 so the fan climbs. Establishes: LL fan index → absolute n calibration; which ν carry the strong gaps (8 vs 16 hierarchy; ν = 4 presence at low B); one vs two SdH ladders (line families converging on the CNP with different slopes); ν = 0 behaviour; hole/electron asymmetry. ~5.5 h.
5. **Fan read + first call draft** in ana: re-formed fan, ν-indexed lines, per-B n-cuts, tone extraction vs n (F(n) slopes summing to h/4e or not), density recalibration.
6. **Decide by the data** (ride the magnet down from 10 T — never re-traverse):
   - if two tone families / ν = 8 hierarchy → ABAB candidate: confirm with a **finite-D fan cut** (D ≈ +0.15 V/nm, hole+electron) — Bernal blocks split differently from a rhombohedral gap;
   - if a single ladder with a 16-fold zero manifold and heavy-mass damping → ABCA candidate: confirm with **T-dependence of the CNP gap at finite D** (`set_both`, ratio 0.95, ≤ 30 K) and of the SdH amplitude at fixed n (mass);
   - if the ladders show a Lifshitz-type change in tone count with n → ABCB candidate: a **dense fixed-n 1/B series** across the transition.
7. **Region B check** (the second series region): the fan carries it as a ×1.13-density replica of every feature; if the replica is resolvable it is the "second region" line of the verdict; otherwise state it as unresolved.
8. **Call** as the ana notebook's last cell (per-region verdict, evidence with run ids and numbers, hedges), then `return-to-initial` close-out.

## What would change my mind / abort criteria for step 4
- First rows: sr1 railing beyond the CNP (≥ 0.9 fs across > 5 points/row) → interrupt, re-size sensitivity. Gate current excess > 100 pA sustained → interrupt (guard trips at 1 nA automatically).
- Rows at 2 T featureless (no minima along n) while runs 6/7 showed oscillations at 2 T → something changed (contacts, T) → stop, re-read state.
- T_sample drifting > 1.5 K at high B → pause (the T-B interaction the rig card flags).
- If by 4 T the fan already reads cleanly (ν-lines indexed, tone families obvious), the high-B half still runs — the ν = 0 / low-ν sector at high B is where ABAB and ABCA differ most.

cat > hera_scratch/ana_spots.py <<'EOF'
"""Runs 6 + 7 (`sdh-spot-check`, D = 0): raw traces, 1/B view, per-tone onsets (sdh_onset), QH-minima filling factors,
and the density-scale check F_(dnu=4) vs F_L(geometry prior). Re-runnable in the ana kernel (uses run(), file_path)."""
from scipy.signal import find_peaks, savgol_filter
from hera.analysis import sdh_onset, SdhOnsetError

h_over_e = cst.h / cst.e   # T m^2
spots = [(6, +3.2, "electron"), (7, -1.2, "hole")]
fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 8))
summary = {}
for k, (rid, n_geo, side) in enumerate(spots):
    g = run(rid)
    B = g.col("magnet_field"); I = g.col("sr0_X") / (-1e6); R = g.col("sr1_X") / I
    o = np.argsort(B); B, R = B[o], R[o]
    FL = luttinger_frequency(abs(n_geo) * 1e16)
    axs[0, k].plot(B, R, lw=0.7); axs[0, k].set_xlabel("B (T)"); axs[0, k].set_ylabel("Rxx (Ohm)")
    axs[0, k].set_title(f"run {rid} — {side}, n_geo = {n_geo:+.1f}e12, D = 0 (raw Rxx)")
    m = B >= 1.0
    axs[1, k].plot(1 / B[m], R[m], lw=0.7); axs[1, k].set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); axs[1, k].set_ylabel("Rxx (Ohm)")
    # QH-like minima above 1.5 T and their filling factor on the geometry-prior density
    Rs = savgol_filter(R[m], 7, 2)
    mins, _ = find_peaks(-Rs, prominence=max(5, 0.05 * Rs.max()))
    Bm, Rm = B[m][mins], Rs[mins]; keep = Bm > 1.5
    nu_geo = abs(n_geo) * 1e16 * h_over_e / Bm
    for b in Bm[keep]: axs[0, k].axvline(b, color="gray", lw=0.4, ls=":")
    print(f"=== run {rid} ({side}): n_geo = {n_geo:+.2f}e12 -> F_L(geo, g=4) = {FL:.1f} T; R(B_min) = {R[0]:.0f} Ohm, max {R.max():.0f} Ohm")
    print("  Rxx minima > 1.5 T: " + ", ".join(f"{b:.2f} T (R {r:.0f}, nu_geo {nu:.1f})" for b, r, nu in zip(Bm[keep], Rm[keep], nu_geo[keep])))
    # spacing of the minima in nu -> Delta-nu = 4 periodicity gives the true density scale
    dnu = -np.diff(nu_geo[keep]); dnu = dnu[(dnu > 2.5) & (dnu < 6)]   # adjacent minima only (skip missed ones)
    scale = 4.0 / np.median(dnu) if len(dnu) else np.nan
    print(f"  adjacent-minima spacing in nu_geo: median {np.median(dnu):.2f} (n={len(dnu)}) -> if these are dnu = 4 gaps, n_true/n_geo = {scale:.3f}")
    try:
        on = sdh_onset(R, B, r_full_scale=50e-6 / 10e-9)
        print(on.summary())
        summary[rid] = on
    except SdhOnsetError as e:
        print("  sdh_onset:", e)
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
EOF

# === Landau fan at D = 0 (`landau-fan`): n fast along the calibrated D = 0 line, B slow 0.5 -> 10 T ===
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD

# --- session calibration from run 5 (cnp-and-dline-calibration; ratio data-calibrated, absolute scale = 9.5 nm prior;
#     runs 6/7 say the scale runs ~10-13 % high — the fan's LL indexing recalibrates it, so n here is "n_geo") ---
CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
n_vec = np.round(np.arange(-1.25, 3.2001, 0.025), 4)          # 1e12 cm^-2, 179 pts, D = 0
Vtg_vec, Vbg_vec = calc_gate_voltages(n_vec, np.zeros_like(n_vec), CAL["c_tg"], CAL["c_bg"], CAL["n_offset"], CAL["D_offset"])
Vtg_vec, Vbg_vec = np.asarray(Vtg_vec, float), np.asarray(Vbg_vec, float)
MARGIN = 0.005   # V — every point strictly inside the committed validators (a throw mid-fan would abort the run)
assert Vtg_vec.min() >= TG_MIN + MARGIN and Vtg_vec.max() <= TG_MAX - MARGIN, (Vtg_vec.min(), Vtg_vec.max())
assert Vbg_vec.min() >= BG_MIN + MARGIN and Vbg_vec.max() <= BG_MAX - MARGIN, (Vbg_vec.min(), Vbg_vec.max())
assert len(Vtg_vec) == len(Vbg_vec) == len(n_vec)
_nchk, _Dchk = calc_nD(Vtg_vec, Vbg_vec, CAL["c_tg"], CAL["c_bg"], CAL["n_offset"], CAL["D_offset"])
assert np.abs(np.asarray(_Dchk)).max() < 1e-6 and np.abs(np.asarray(_nchk) - n_vec).max() < 1e-6
print(f"fast axis: n_geo {n_vec[0]:+.3f} .. {n_vec[-1]:+.3f}e12 ({len(n_vec)} pts, 0.025 step) at D = 0 -> "
      f"Vtg [{Vtg_vec.min():+.4f}, {Vtg_vec.max():+.4f}] V, Vbg [{Vbg_vec.min():+.4f}, {Vbg_vec.max():+.4f}] V "
      f"(validators TG [{TG_MIN}, {TG_MAX}], BG [{BG_MIN}, {BG_MAX}])")

# --- slow axis: uniform-B rows, denser where the fan converges ---
B_vec = np.unique(np.round(np.hstack((np.arange(0.5, 4.0001, 0.1), np.arange(4.2, 10.0001, 0.2))), 3))   # 66 rows, climbing
assert B_vec.max() <= B_SESSION_CAP and B_vec.min() > 0
print(f"slow axis: B {B_vec[0]} -> {B_vec[-1]} T, {len(B_vec)} rows (0.1 T to 4 T, 0.2 T above)")

# --- preconditions (assumed, not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0, _B0 = T_sample(), magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (|B| < 0.05: fan climbs from 0), V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (0), "
      f"nplci tg/bg = {k_tg.nplci()}/{k_bg.nplci()} (1/1), PS heater {magnet.persistent_switch_on()}, output {magnet.output_enabled()}")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5 and abs(_B0) < 0.05 and abs(k_si()) < 0.01
assert k_tg.nplci() == 1 and k_bg.nplci() == 1
assert magnet.persistent_switch_on() and magnet.output_enabled()

# --- lock-in settling: tau 0.3 -> 0.1 s on both lock-ins so fast_delay 1.0 s = 10 tau (24 dB/oct settles to 1 % in ~10 tau);
#     at tau 0.3 s the same dwell leaves ~half of each step unsettled and smears LL minima over ~3 fast points.
#     Acquisition setting, not a safety surface; state0 (close-out restore) holds the operator's 0.3 s.
print(f"tau before: sr0 {sr0.time_constant()} s, sr1 {sr1.time_constant()} s; slope sr1 {sr1.filter_slope()} dB/oct")
sr0.time_constant(0.1); sr1.time_constant(0.1)
# Fixed sensitivity for the whole fan (no autorange mid-row): 100 uV = 10 kOhm FS at 10 nA; CNP at high B may rail (that is a read).
sr1.sensitivity(100e-6)
FAST_DELAY, SLOW_DELAY = 1.0, 3.0
I_TRIP = 1e-9
print(f"tau after: sr0 {sr0.time_constant()} s, sr1 {sr1.time_constant()} s; drive {sr1.amplitude()} V -> 10 nA; "
      f"sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V (10 kOhm FS); sr0 sens {sr0.sensitivity()} V; fast_delay {FAST_DELAY} s")

mc = dict(meas_config); mc["Si (V)"] = k_si(); mc["sample_temperature:"] = _T0
mc["comments"] = (f"landau-fan D=0: n_geo fast {n_vec[0]:+.3f}..{n_vec[-1]:+.3f}e12 ({len(n_vec)} pts) along D = 0 (run-5 cal), "
                  f"B slow {B_vec[0]}->{B_vec[-1]} T ({len(B_vec)} rows: 0.1 T to 4 T, 0.2 T above), Vsi = 0, sr1 100 uV, tau 0.1 s")
s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
s.add_comment('landau-fan')
s.add_comment(f'D = 0 line (run-5 cal: ratio {CAL["c_bg"]/CAL["c_tg"]:.3f}, c_tg {CAL["c_tg"]:.3e} prior anchor, n_offset {CAL["n_offset"]:+.4f}e12, '
              f'D_offset {CAL["D_offset"]:+.3f} V/nm); fast (Vtg, Vbg) co-swept, n_geo {n_vec[0]:+.3f}..{n_vec[-1]:+.3f}e12 step 0.025 ({len(n_vec)} pts); '
              f'slow B {B_vec[0]}..{B_vec[-1]} T, {len(B_vec)} rows; fast_delay {FAST_DELAY} s, slow_delay {SLOW_DELAY} s; tau 0.1 s; sr1 100 uV')

# park the gates at the row start, then climb to the first field row (both blocking)
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, Vbg_vec[0]); s.ramp(k_tg.volt, Vtg_vec[0])
interruptible_sleep(5)
s.ramp(magnet.field, B_vec[0])
interruptible_sleep(5)

# row layout: [time, B(slow), Vtg(fast), Vbg(fast), T_sample, k_tg.curr, k_bg.curr, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr1.X); s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr0.X)
s.plot('time', k_tg.curr); s.plot('time', k_bg.curr)

def leak_guard(station, data):
    i_tg, i_bg = abs(float(data[5])), abs(float(data[6]))
    if i_tg > I_TRIP or i_bg > I_TRIP:
        print(f"LEAK TRIP at B={float(data[1]):+.3f} T, Vtg={float(data[2]):+.4f}, Vbg={float(data[3]):+.4f}: |I_tg|={i_tg:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg:.3e} A")
        station.interrupt_requested = True
s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtg_vec, Vbg_vec],
                 slow_delay=SLOW_DELAY, fast_delay=FAST_DELAY, init_delay=False)
# field stays at 10 T (the next step rides it down), gates stay at the last fast point — no park here.
print(f"done: B = {magnet.field():+.3f} T, (Vtg, Vbg) = ({k_tg.volt():+.4f}, {k_bg.volt():+.4f}), T_sample = {T_sample():.3f} K")

## HERA — Step 4: Landau fan at D = 0 (`landau-fan`), n −1.25 … +3.2×10¹² × B 0.5 → 10 T

**Why now (plan step 4; operator request).** Runs 6/7 (ana) show clean SdH from ~1 T and QH minima with Rxx → 0 by 2.3 T on the electron side; the Δν = 4 periodicity there sits at F ≈ 29.5 T against F_L(geo) = 33.1 T, so the 9.5 nm-anchored density scale runs ~10 % high and both spot checks carry ambiguous ν assignments (hole side: minima at ν_geo ≈ 10, 8.3, 7.1, 5.9). The fan resolves all of it at once: LL lines indexed by ν give the absolute n calibration; **which ν carry the strong gaps** (ν = 8 hierarchy → Bernal blocks; ν = 16 first, then 4/8/12 → rhombohedral manifold; ν = 4 at low B → a Dirac-like block, ABCB); **one vs two line families** converging on the CNP (two bilayer-like Fermi surfaces vs one); and the ν = 0 / low-ν sector at high B where ABAB and ABCA differ most. Region B (0.43×10¹² electron-doped, run 5) should appear as a ×1.13-density replica of every feature.

**Design.** Fast axis: (V_tg, V_bg) co-swept along the run-5 D = 0 line, n_geo −1.25 → +3.2×10¹² in 0.025 steps (179 pts; TG −0.291 … +0.984 V, BG −0.484 … +1.166 V, ≥ 5 mV inside every validator — the full D = 0 window the operating box allows; the hole side is TG-limited at −1.27).
